---
title: "How to Store NASA Credentials as Environment Variables in R (Rproj)"
format: pdf
editor: visual
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(blackmarbler)
```

## 1. Create or open a `.Renviron` file

If you want the variables to apply **only to your current R project**, run:

```{r}
#| eval: false
file.edit(".Renviron")
```

This will create (or open) a `.Renviron` file inside your project folder (same level as the `.Rproj` file).

If you want them available in **all R projects**, run instead:

```{r}
#| eval: false
file.edit("~/.Renviron")
```

## 2. Add your credentials

Inside the `.Renviron` file, write:

```         
NASA_USERNAME=your_username 
NASA_PASSWORD=your_password
```

Important:

-   No spaces around `=`

-   Do not use quotes

Save the file.

## 3. Restart RStudio

Close and reopen RStudio. This step is required for the variables to load.

## 4. Use the variables in your script

Now you can safely call:

```{r}
#| eval: false

bearer <- get_nasa_token(
    username = Sys.getenv("NASA_USERNAME"),
    password = Sys.getenv("NASA_PASSWORD")
)

nchar(bearer)
```

## 5. (Optional) Check that it works

```{r}
#| eval: false
Sys.getenv("NASA_USERNAME")
```

If it prints your username, everything is set correctly.
